text:
sara-support: FYI — customer AcmeData reports sustained 429s from /v1/embeddings during their nightly bulk job. Started at ~02:12 UTC, job sends batches of 512 with concurrency 40. Some responses include Retry-After: 5, others return plain 429. Also seeing occasional 'dimension mismatch' on ~0.1% of rows. Need triage and quick mitigations.
anna-customer: their job config: batch_size=512, workers=40 (aiohttp), model=text-embedding-3-small. 500k rows, runs every night. logs: "429 {\"error\":{\"type\":\"rate_limit\",\"message\":\"rate limit exceeded\"}}" and sometimes "{\"error\":{\"message\":\"dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 768\"}}". We'll share request_ids if needed.
mike-eng: can you paste a sample response with headers (especially Retry-After) and a request_id? also confirm whether they use a single API key for the whole job or rotate keys per worker.
anna-customer: sample (redacted):
```http
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
Retry-After: 5
Request-Id: req_8b9f2a
{
  "error": {"type":"rate_limit","message":"rate limit exceeded"}
}
```
We use one shared API key across workers.
leo-oncall: immediate mitigation suggestions:
- reduce concurrency: 40 -> 6-8
- reduce batch_size: 512 -> 128 (or test 256)
- add exponential backoff + full jitter on 429s (base 1s, cap 60s)
- shard the job across time windows (stagger start times)
These should stop the 429 flood while we investigate.
jordan-ml: on the dimension mismatch: that error suggests some inputs were encoded with a different model or the pipeline appended/trimmed vectors. text-embedding-3-small expects 1536 dims; 768 would be from some older/smaller model. Ask the customer to verify model param on every worker and that they didn't accidentally mix outputs from previous runs.
mike-eng: couple of asks for deeper debug:
- provide 10 request_ids that hit 429 + the full response headers for each
- share a short trace of worker process (pid, python package versions, client lib version)
- confirm whether they are running from a single region (us-west1) or multi-region — cross-region can generate transient routing rate limits
anna-customer: collecting request ids now, here's a small sample: req_8b9f2a, req_8b9f3c, req_8b9f4d. All from us-west1. Using our in-house wrapper around requests v2.31.
ops-bot: ratecap alert: embedding_global_rps exceeded by key (key=acct-xxxx). threshold=200rps sustained, burst=1500 over 10s window. Generated incident id INC-8742.
leo-oncall: ops-bot confirms global ratecap hit. two follow-ups:
1) short-term: we can temporarily raise burst window for this key by 2x if Legal approves (manual action). not ideal.
2) medium-term: recommend customer move to Dedicated (reserved capacity) for sustained 100s rps; or implement client-side throttling.
I'll also ask infra to check if any request routing anomalies occurred at 02:10-02:20 UTC.
mike-eng: for our internal debugging please gather:
- server-side logs around those request_ids (I'll open an internal trace request)
- whether any embed-serving nodes reported OOM or queue backpressure
I'll take the request_ids once you post them.
anna-customer: we've set concurrency=8 and batch_size=128 and added backoff + jitter. Rerunning tonight and will report. If still bad we'll open for Dedicated.
jordan-ml: for the dimension check: recommend a quick client-side assert before sending:
```python
vec = client.embed(texts, model="text-embedding-3-small")
for v in vec:
    assert len(v) == 1536, f"wrong dim: {len(v)}"
```
Also check any cached embeddings you might be concatenating — that can mix dims.
deploy-bot: created support ticket SUP-123456 and internal incident INC-8742. assigned to @mike-eng and @leo-oncall.
leo-oncall: follow-up actions:
- mike: collect server logs for req ids and check rate-limiter traces
- sara: offer customer a best-practice doc for large embed jobs (throttling, batching, dedupe) and link to Dedicated onboarding
- ops: confirm whether we can do a temporary burst lift and list required approvals
sara-support: will send the doc and the quick mitigation checklist to AcmeData now. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
